name_reason: Already compliant: data_fd2_ prefix, battle core-table domain, descriptor ai_best_spell_score accurately reflects the AI offensive-spell best-candidate score accumulator. No Ghidra address residue (0x53c23 not present as a trailing hex; descriptor is purely semantic). Scalar accumulator data type is reflected by 'score'.
purpose: Battle AI offensive-spell planner scratch: holds the best (signed max) candidate score found while scoring every castable spell over every reachable cast tile.
logic_summary: fd2_ai_score_offensive_spell @0x1598A resets it to 0 at entry (MOV [0x53C23],0 @0x1599B), then for each (spell x cast-tile) candidate compares the candidate score against it (CMP+JG signed @0x15AE2) and on a strict win (tie-broken by spell base damage) stores the new best (MOV [0x53C23],EDX @0x15AF5) together with the paired target_x @0x53C27 / target_y @0x53C2B / spell_id @0x53C2F. Readers (fd2_attack_action_dispatch, fd2_enemy_turn_action_dispatcher, fd2_enemy_turn_phase_team0, fd2_execute_ai_offensive_spell) read it as a full signed dword (compared against 6 and the sibling physical/item scores) to choose the winning enemy action.
element_semantics: Single signed 32-bit scalar = best offensive-spell candidate score accumulator (signed max). Candidate scores are small positive priority sums produced by fd2_score_spell_candidate (e.g. 8 / 0x18 per target). Zero-initialized BSS (memory reads all zeros).
notes: Confirmed NOT const: two game-side write-xrefs in fd2_ai_score_offensive_spell (init @0x1599B, store-best @0x15AF5); correctly emitted as non-const int32. Signed semantics confirmed by JG @0x15AE2 and signed dword compares in readers. src comment block (btl_aisc.c lines 626-633) already accurate and concise -> not edited (only the shard file is staged). Ghidra data plate at 0x53C23 was empty (null) -> created a concise plate via PLATE_COMMENT consistent with the src conclusion (verified read-back SET_OK). run_script_inline output also showed unrelated pre-existing stale .java compile errors in ghidra_scripts dir; my inline script itself compiled and ran fine.
